name: Thumb pulling

card.summary: Pulling the palate downward with a thumb to widen the upper jaw; discussed as a free substitute for expanders, with no studies behind it.
card.note: No clinical study exists; the midpalatal suture generally fuses after puberty, and users report tooth gaps in combined regimens.

quick.overview:
Thumb pulling is a looksmaxxing practice in which a person places a thumb on the roof of the mouth and pulls downward and forward, intending to widen or move the upper jaw. It is presented in forums as a do-it-yourself imitation of the palate expanders used in orthodontics.

Proponents report easier breathing, a feeling of movement in the maxilla and a larger palate. Other forum users call it ineffective, and no published study has tested it.
quick.mechanism: The idea is that sustained mechanical force on the palate remodels bone, as in orthodontic expansion. Orthodontic expansion uses fixed appliances that apply controlled force over weeks, and in teenagers and adults the midpalatal suture is generally less open or fused, which is why implant-assisted or surgical expansion is used. Forum users themselves question whether a thumb can produce enough force for long enough.
quick.risks: No clinical safety data exist. Orthodontic literature on expansion lists side effects such as a gap between the upper front teeth, pain and bone thinning, but those concern appliances. Forum posts describe diastema after combining thumb pulling with hard mewing and expanders.

lead: Thumb pulling is a practice in looksmaxxing communities in which a person pulls on the palate with the thumb, usually downward and forward, in the belief that it can widen the palate or move the maxilla forward [1][2]. It is discussed as a free alternative to professional palatal expansion and is commonly paired with mewing and chewing.

No published study has tested thumb pulling. Professional palatal expansion, by contrast, is an established orthodontic procedure that uses appliances, usually in children and adolescents, because the midpalatal suture is open early in life and generally fuses after puberty [3].

paras: Forum threads describe placing a thumb against the palate and pulling, with questions about exactly where on the palate to place the thumb [4]. Related threads discuss thumb pulling for underbites and maxilla growth, and whether a second person could do the pulling [5][6][7].

Rapid palatal expansion uses a device the patient turns to widen the palate roughly 0.5 to 1 mm per day, typically left in for three to six months, and is mostly done in children and adolescents aged about 8 to 18 [3]. In adults the suture generally requires surgery or implant assistance, and side effects include speech changes, pain, tongue sores and a gap between the upper front teeth [3]. Treatment after the growth spurt is described as mainly moving teeth rather than changing bone [3].
No studies found. No published trial or case series has tested thumb pulling. Research on palatal expansion concerns orthodontic appliances, not manual pulling [3].

On looksmax.org, one user said that after being told the method was 'cope' with no results, he saw a change after a week of twice-daily thumb pulling with hard mewing, reporting a larger palate on one side and easier breathing [1]. Another asked whether it works and said they could breathe better after two weeks, while a reply said thumb pulling works in theory but that a thumb cannot generate enough force for long enough, calling it a diluted version of an expander [2]. A third thread's replies suggest it no longer works after about age 15 to 16, while a 17-year-old described feeling something in the maxilla [8]. Other threads report no progress after three months [9], a gap between the front teeth after expansion combined with thumb pulling [10], and straighter noses attributed to chewing and thumb pulling [11].

lore.intro: Thumb pulling is treated as a low-cost add-on to mewing, with members divided on whether it does anything [1][2][8].

claims.claim: Thumb pulling can widen the palate or advance the maxilla
claims.believers: Users report a feeling of movement in the maxilla, better suction of the tongue and improved breathing after days to weeks [1][2][8].
claims.experts: No published studies have tested it. Orthodontic expansion works through appliances and is described as most effective before or during the growth spurt [3].

claims.claim: It only works before about 15 or 16
claims.believers: Forum replies say it is 'cope' past that age, while a 17-year-old disagrees [8].
claims.experts: The midpalatal suture is open in children and generally fuses after puberty, so adult expansion usually needs surgery or implant assistance [3].

claims.claim: A thumb cannot generate enough force to matter
claims.believers: A forum user says it works in theory but not in practice, describing it as a diluted expander [2].
claims.experts: No published measurement exists of the force produced by thumb pulling.

claims.claim: Thumb pulling can create a diastema or other tooth changes
claims.believers: A thread asks what to do about a gap between the front teeth after expansion, thumb pulling and hard mewing [10].
claims.experts: A diastema is a recognised side effect of orthodontic palatal expansion [3].
